bug_description.normalized: While HarfBuzz sanitizes and later applies the staged font's AAT `morx` table, chain subtable 5 carries a malformed Format-2 class lookup whose header advertises `unitSize=1` and `nUnits=4` for `LookupSegmentSingle<HBUINT16>` elements. Vulnerable `VarSizedBinSearchArrayOf::sanitize_shallow()` accepts that undersized stride, so the malformed lookup survives font sanitization and remains available at shaping time. On the crashing run, a current-insert action later executes `buffer->copy_glyph()` without proving that `buffer->info[idx]` names an initialized glyph, and MemorySanitizer traces the copied uninitialized `hb_glyph_info_t.codepoint` forward into a later `StateTable::get_class` call. That later class lookup selects the retained Format-2 table, `LookupFormat2::get_value()` binary-searches it, and `LookupSegmentSingle::cmp()` consumes the uninitialized glyph id, triggering use-of-uninitialized-value. The saved artifacts do not identify the exact intervening state row or entry that makes the copied record current again, but they do prove both the `copy_glyph()` store and the later Format-2 sink.

source.code: return_trace (header.sanitize (c) && Type::static_size >= header.unitSize && c->check_array (bytesZ.arrayZ, header.nUnits, header.unitSize));
source.description: First verified project statement on the crashing path that consumes attacker-controlled `morx` bytes and creates vulnerability-relevant state. Static decoding of the staged PoC's chain subtable 5 shows a Format-2 class lookup with `unitSize = 1` and `nUnits = 4`; this vulnerable check accepts that undersized stride for `LookupSegmentSingle<HBUINT16>` elements, so the malformed lookup survives sanitization and remains reachable at the later sink.
source.value_from: The staged `poc`'s `morx` chain subtable 5 class table decodes to `format = 2`, `unitSize = 1`, `nUnits = 4`. The staged patch flips this exact comparison to `Type::static_size <= header.unitSize`, which would reject that header.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `cmp()` consumes the uninitialized glyph id `g` that was copied by `copy_glyph()` and later forwarded through `StateTable::get_class`, `Lookup::get_value`, and `LookupFormat2::get_value` into the malformed Format-2 class-table binary search.

root_cause.description: Runtime origin of the uninitialized value. The current-insert path calls `copy_glyph()` whenever `CurrentInsertBefore` is clear, but it never proves that `buffer->idx` still names an initialized input glyph before reading `info[idx]`. The saved MSAN origin chain shows that this exact call copied a never-initialized `hb_glyph_info_t` from the spare buffer capacity created by `hb_buffer_t::enlarge`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged PoC's `morx` chain contains insertion subtables (`coverage & 0xff == 5`), so shaping dispatches into `InsertionSubtable::apply` on attacker-controlled table bytes.
parser_admitted.condition: Static decoding of the staged `poc` shows all 11 chain subtables have type `Insertion` (coverage low byte `0x05`), matching the runtime stack frame at `AAT::ChainSubtable::dispatch` line 786.

format2_class_lookup_retained.description: The malformed class lookup stays attached to the insertion state machine because `classTable.sanitize(c, this)` succeeds under the vulnerable shallow-size check from step 1.
format2_class_lookup_retained.condition: For chain subtable 5, the staged PoC decodes to `format = 2`, `unitSize = 1`, `nUnits = 4`; with the vulnerable `>=` comparison this lookup is admitted, while the staged patch's `<=` comparison would reject it.

tainted_value_origin.description: The glyph-info buffer is grown with `realloc` and the newly added spare slots are left uninitialized. MSAN's heap origin points back to this allocation path, and the later `copy_glyph()` read pulls bytes from that never-written spare capacity.

fine_trace.code: return_trace (header.sanitize (c) && Type::static_size >= header.unitSize && c->check_array (bytesZ.arrayZ, header.nUnits, header.unitSize));
fine_trace.note: Static decoding of the staged PoC's chain subtable 5 yields a Format-2 class lookup with `unitSize = 1` and `nUnits = 4`. Because this vulnerable check uses `Type::static_size >= header.unitSize`, HarfBuzz accepts that undersized `LookupSegmentSingle<HBUINT16>` stride instead of rejecting it, so the malformed lookup survives to runtime.

fine_trace.code: if (entry->data.currentInsertIndex != 0xFFFF) { unsigned int count = (flags & CurrentInsertCount) >> 5; unsigned int start = entry->data.currentInsertIndex; const GlyphID *glyphs = &insertionAction[start]; if (unlikely (!c->sanitizer.check_array (glyphs, count))) return false; }
fine_trace.note: The crashing run enters the current-insert block of an insertion subtable. The saved MSAN store stack reaches line 648 inside this block, so `entry->data.currentInsertIndex != 0xFFFF` was true for the executed transition, even though the exact subtable index and entry number are not statically recoverable from the staged artifacts.

The crashing execution takes the `!before` arm. That is source-grounded by the executed call at line 648: `buffer->copy_glyph()` only runs when `CurrentInsertBefore` is clear, so `before` is false for the faulting transition.

Missing guard: once `before` is false, the current-insert path calls `copy_glyph()` without checking that `buffer->idx` still designates an initialized glyph record. The saved MSAN origin proves that this executed call read from never-initialized spare buffer capacity.

This statement materializes the uninitialized value. MSAN traces the copied bytes back to the spare `hb_glyph_info_t` capacity created by `hb_buffer_t::enlarge`, showing that `info[idx]` had never been initialized before being copied into the output span.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int klass = buffer->idx < buffer->len ? machine.get_class (buffer->info[buffer->idx].codepoint, num_glyphs) : (unsigned) StateTable<EntryData>::CLASS_END_OF_TEXT;
fine_trace.note: Later on the same shaping path, the copied uninitialized `codepoint` is re-materialized as the `glyph_id` consumed by `machine.get_class()`. The saved MSAN store chain proves the value stored by step 5 reaches this call, but the exact intervening state-table row or entry that made the copied record current again is not recoverable from the staged artifacts.
`get_class()` uses the uninitialized `glyph_id` from step 6 as the lookup key and consults the attacker-controlled class table that step 1 allowed to survive sanitization.

fine_trace.code: switch (u.format) { case 0: return u.format0.get_value (glyph_id, num_glyphs); case 2: return u.format2.get_value (glyph_id); default: return nullptr; }
fine_trace.note: The retained class table begins with `format = 2`, so `Lookup::get_value()` dispatches this key into the Format-2 lookup arm rather than another lookup encoding.
The Format-2 lookup begins a binary search over the malformed segment array using the uninitialized `glyph_id` as the key.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int size = header.unitSize; ... const Type *p = (const Type *) (((const char *) &bytesZ) + (mid * size)); int c = p->cmp (key);
fine_trace.note: Runtime use of the malformed header from step 1: `bsearch()` uses the attacker-controlled `unitSize = 1` as the stride when reinterpreting the segment bytes as `LookupSegmentSingle<HBUINT16>` records before calling `cmp(key)`.
MSAN reports use-of-uninitialized-value here because `cmp()` consumes the uninitialized glyph id forwarded from step 6 as `g` during the Format-2 segment comparison.

allocation_context.note: The MSAN heap origin is the spare `hb_glyph_info_t` capacity allocated by `realloc` in `hb_buffer_t::enlarge`, reached from `hb_buffer_add_utf8` while the harness loads the fixed UTF-8 string.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partial - the MSAN heap origin is the spare buffer slot allocated in `hb_buffer_t::enlarge`, and the runtime root cause is the later unguarded `copy_glyph()` read of that slot. The staged patch resolves the saved PoC by rejecting the malformed Format-2 class table during sanitization, not by changing `copy_glyph()` itself.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes - runtime fine-trace steps 2 through 11 align with the saved MSAN stack and origin chain; step 1 is an earlier parse-time sanitizer admission fact established from the staged source, patch, and PoC bytes rather than a crash-stack frame.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Static decoding of the staged `poc` shows that the later sink uses chain subtable 5's Format-2 class lookup with `unitSize = 1` and `nUnits = 4`. The staged patch changes `VarSizedBinSearchArrayOf::sanitize_shallow()` from `Type::static_size >= header.unitSize` to `Type::static_size <= header.unitSize`, which would reject that malformed lookup during sanitization and prevent the saved crash path from being admitted. This is a source-level conclusion; no fixed-runtime execution is staged here.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: One staged vulnerable run reproduced the issue and the saved MSAN trace independently records the same `copy_glyph()` origin and `LookupFormat2`/`cmp` sink chain. No fixed run or second detector trace is available in this Stage 02 workspace.

format.name: sfnt font with AAT morx table
format.contract: An sfnt font whose `morx` table includes the malformed insertion-subtable class lookup decoded from the staged PoC (chain subtable 5 carries a Format-2 class table with `unitSize = 1` and `nUnits = 4`) and that, when HarfBuzz shapes the harness string `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`, reaches a current-insert `copy_glyph()` call that copies a never-initialized `hb_glyph_info_t` later consumed as `glyph_id` by that Format-2 class lookup.
